subject: Pilot capacity ask: dedicated slab & autoscale exception
messages:
From: Ana Caballero <ana.caballero@ed-systems.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Dedicated GPU allocation for May pilot (requirements attached)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We want to move forward with a 3-week pilot starting the week of May 22. Before we lock dates, we need confirmation on two things: a dedicated slab of capacity on Redwood Dedicated and an autoscale policy exception so our traffic spike patterns (short bursts to 300 qps, median sequence length ~512 tokens) don't get preempted.

High-level ask:
- Dedicated slab: baseline of ~8 concurrent slots (equiv. 2x A100-80GB) reserved during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT) for 21 days.
- Autoscale exception: allow burst headroom up to 12 concurrent during pilot without triggering preemption/gating rules.
- Billing: we expect a short-term monthly commit to cover the pilot.

Attached is an initial requirements workbook with our expected traffic patterns and input sizes. Can you confirm whether this is feasible and what the exception path/process looks like? We may need a signed SOW and an ops runbook.

CC'ing Ethan (CTO) — he may chime in on technical constraints.

Thanks,
Ana
Ana Caballero
Head of Infrastructure, Ed Systems
[attachment: ed-systems-pilot-requirements.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Caballero <ana.caballero@ed-systems.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-15T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated GPU allocation for May pilot (requirements attached)

Hi Ana — great to see this moving quickly. Welcome, and thanks for the clear workbook. We're confident we can support the pilot shape but will need a brief cross-functional exception to our autoscale policy and a short reservation on a dedicated pool.

Proposed next steps (quick):
1) 30-minute alignment call this week to validate concurrency and traffic burst windows. Suggested times: Thu 10:00 PT or Fri 11:30 PT.
2) Engineering/Infra (Jonas) to confirm exact GPU equivalence and isolation implications.
3) Product/legal to prepare a short SOW and a 21-day reservation clause (Tessa/Kimberly).

Operationally, our preferred path is: temporary slab carved from a pilot pool + autoscale override for 21 days with telemetry gating. During the period we'll monitor token-level cost and latency; if we see >10% regression on other tenants, we will mutually agree on mitigations.

I've started a mutual action plan draft and attached version 0.1 — please review and let me know which proposed time works. Also confirm: does Ed Systems need any on-prem or VPC-only isolation, or is the dedicated pooled slice acceptable?

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[attachment: MAP-edsystems-v1.docx (docx)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-16T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated GPU allocation for May pilot (requirements attached)

Tessa / team — dug into the workbook. Quick notes/risks:
- Concurrency shape (~8 baseline, bursts to 12) maps to around 2 full A100-80GB equivalents with aggressive KV cache usage. We can satisfy this from the pilot pool but it reduces available opportunistic capacity for other pilots.
- Autoscale exception: we can implement an exception token that raises the soft cap for this customer for 21 days, but it requires a manual policy flip and an operator watch for the first 72 hours.
- Sequence length 512 is heavier than most pilots — expect higher per-token throughput cost; we should ensure accounting is clear in the SOW.

Operational recommendation:
- Approve a 21-day temporary carve (business hours, 08:00-20:00 PT) for 2 GPU equivalents.
- Autoscale exception enabled with manual rollback criteria: sustained 5-minute tail latency >2x baseline or cluster token saturation >85%.
- Runbook: oncall to monitor KPIs, automatic alerts to infra-ops and product (link below).

I'll prepare the operator runbook snippet and post to INFRA-3245. If product/legal want to proceed, we can sign off on the exception by Friday to meet the May 22 start.

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook-edsystems-brief.md (md)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated GPU allocation for May pilot (requirements attached)

Team — decision: approve temporary reservation and autoscale exception for Ed Systems as follows.

Approved scope:
- Dedicated slab: carve out 2 GPU-equivalent slots (approx. 8 concurrent baseline) from the pilot pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT) for 21 days starting May 22.
- Autoscale exception: allow burst headroom up to 12 concurrent for the 21-day pilot. Exception will be enforced with operator monitoring and the rollback criteria Jonas specified.
- Billing: finance will require a short-term commit; draft SOW to capture overage pricing.

Operational asks to enact this:
- Jonas: finalize and link the runbook to INFRA-3245 and set the first 72-hour oncall watch schedule.
- Laura/CS: update customer MAP and confirm billing commit with Ed Systems (use deal RID-4579).
- Tessa: coordinate SOW signature and routing to Legal; attach DocuSign link in the MAP.

I'm attaching the approval notice for records. We should capture the exception in the exceptions register and schedule a retro at pilot end.

Thanks all — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
[attachment: dedicated-exception-approval.pdf (pdf)]
